differences.what: T-2564: the north return is laid in large dressed courses (about 0.46 m) with staggered joints, 5.5 m long as the course counts in the 1887-89 and 1948 views give it, where it was a smooth 2.8 m slab.

T-2564: the pinnacle caps are ogival with a moulded collar and ball finial, the rear one seated on the coping, and the rounded coping sweeps up into the corner pinnacle on the return and at both front corners.
Most of Keith is occluded by Glessner or outside this frame. Its bow, stair, lower ornament and rear cannot be accepted from this view. The isolated render does not include the occluding neighbour.
The original is monochrome; granite colour is not shown. Sepia/scan casts are not material colour.

T-2578: the cowl ventilator stands on the deck behind the return, a galvanized pipe inclined forward from just inside the rear pinnacle to an upright neck under a bowl and a broad disc; its height over the coping against the rear pinnacle's agrees with the picture.

T-2578 ruling: the stone parapet stops at the rear pinnacle. Every picture that sees that corner (1887, Taylor 2135, the 1888 Glessner plate, the c. 1888 view looking SW, the Glessner front, 1948) shows sky straight behind it, or in 1948 a darker wall about a course lower; the model drops it there.

T-2577: the cornice box under the lattice is laid in the front's dressed stone, so the crown reads as one stone mass from the wall head to the lattice, as the photographs show it; the brown band is gone in this render.

T-2578: the hall stack stands over the coping beside the ventilator, where this picture shows sky; the stack should stop below the coping, the cowl pipe plausibly being its flue's termination (left for T-2580). T-2712: fixed — the hall stack now stops at 16.1 m, under the return's coping, and the render shows sky over the coping beside the cowl as the picture does; the cowl's pipe rises from the stack's top.
T-2578: the ventilator's pipe reads pale beside the granite, as the print shows it (the colour itself is reconstructed: the print is monochrome).

T-2714: the checker band's units are pitched 0.28 m along their rows (0.336 m before), with 0.07 m of ground between neighbours, as the 1888 Keith plate lays them; the rows are unchanged. Not judged here: only the north return's crown shows here, edge-on.

T-2813: re-rendered with Keith's crown 0.16 m lower (the moulded course under the lattice 0.20 m deep where it was 0.36 m, the checker and head bands unmoved); its camera does not use the crown and is unchanged. Read again at the crown beside the previous render: the lattice, coping and pinnacles move a few pixels at this picture's scale and nothing it shows opens a difference; the verdict stands as it was (matches).

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown}. A ticket whose ## Image gate names this building does not close while it is not "matches" (tools/image_gate.mjs).
